property_summary: Calling AdjustBetAmounts(amount) sets currentBetLimit() to amount (i.e., it overwrites the previous limit rather than adding to it).

After calling AdjustBetAmounts(amount) once, the contract's currentBetLimit() is nonzero whenever the provided amount is nonzero (i.e., setting bet limit to a nonzero value), assuming prior limit can be anything.
When the owner sets the bet limit to a nonzero amount, the contract's currentBetLimit() becomes equal to that provided amount.
If owner sets bet limit to a value greater than or equal to the current limit, the contract's bet limit after the call is at least that value.

property_summary: Calling AdjustBetAmounts(amount) always results in betLimit being exactly equal to the provided amount (i.e., it sets, not increments); the mutant that adds instead will make betLimit differ for some amounts (when previous betLimit != 0).

Only the owner can change the bet limit (so calling AdjustBetAmounts from the original owner leaves betLimit unchanged when owner calls with same owner address), i.e., when invoked by the contract-deployer-owner the bet limit equals the passed amount only if the caller is the owner (original holds: owner can change it; mutant forbids owner).

OnlyOwner modifier in P prevents non-owner from successfully calling AdjustBetAmounts, so when called by msg.sender equal to the deployer (owner) AdjustBetAmounts must revert if play() already caused a state that makes owner disallowed — more generally, calling AdjustBetAmounts from the same address that called play() must revert in P but may succeed in M.

If the caller address is equal to the contract's deployer (the owner) then calling AdjustBetAmounts must revert when invoked immediately after that same address called play(), but a caller that is different from the deployer may succeed.

When the caller is the contract owner, calling AdjustBetAmounts should revert (original onlyOwner requires msg.sender == owner; mutant inverts and allows the owner), so for any caller equal to the deployer/owner, AdjustBetAmounts must revert after that caller has called play().
When the caller is the contract owner, calling AdjustBetAmounts reverts (i.e., owner cannot successfully call AdjustBetAmounts) after that same caller invoked play() on the contract.
After calling AdjustDifficulty(amount) once from initial difficulty d0, currentDifficulty() equals d0 + amount only if AdjustDifficulty replaces; it must NOT grow faster than amount when called once.

property_summary: For any caller who is the contract owner, calling OpenToThePublic() sets c.currentBetLimit()'s corresponding boolean openToPublic to true in the reference, so after the call the contract's openToPublic getter (accessed via attempting a wager which requires openToPublic) will allow public actions; the mutant flips the flag to false and thus for some fuzzed owner address the public action will be disallowed — we assert that an owner can enable public actions (wager succeeds) after OpenToThePublic is called.

After the owner calls OpenToThePublic, the contract should allow a real EOA to call wager (i.e., hasPlayerWagered becomes true) for any nonzero betLimit and an EOA paying exactly betLimit; the mutant that flips the flag prevents this for some inputs.

After the contract owner calls OpenToThePublic(), the contract should allow a non-owner EOA to successfully call wager() (which requires openToPublic==true) when sending exactly the bet limit; the mutant that sets openToPublic = false breaks this by disallowing such a wager for some fuzzed actor/amount.
